notes: Two supplied object its are added; neither clause writes an object morpheme (rule 44).
The explicit ʾattāh takes thyself while the verb keeps its own thou, and lə-baddekā is fused as alone (rule 30).
ʾittəkā is the preposition ʾēt with, not the object marker, and its unit is discontinuous from the verb (rules 16, 25).
